$comment: MACHINE-DEFINABLE ANSWERS ONLY. Do not add a mark here for footage a person has to look at.
testdata/groundtruth.json is the HUMAN review and its $comment forbids filling it with a number
without somebody having looked at the footage. That rule is not weakened here; it is why this
file exists separately. A mark in THIS file is one whose correct answer is derivable from the
clip itself, with no judgement: the detector was told to find a thing that is or is not in the
frame, so the answer is in the frame and not in anybody's opinion.
Two of the three committed clips qualify. `car-crossing.mp4` does NOT: a real car on a real
road is a judgement call about what counts as a crossing, and nobody has watched it, so it has
no mark in either file and `pocctl report` says so.
KEYED BY CLIP, NOT BY TAG. The human file is keyed by `tag`, because a person reads a review
sheet printed from one run and writes the tags off it. Tags are generated per run, so a
committed file cannot carry them. This file is keyed by the committed clip name, and
`pocctl adjudicate` resolves a clip to this run's own pushed tags through `detections.clip_ref`,
so the join is the SAME join `pocctl mark` uses and a mark still cannot land on an event that
A mark that resolves to nothing is reported as unresolved and NOT counted. The precision figure
is over what was counted, and the count of what was not is printed beside it -- a rate for a
smaller review than the file holds is the failure this whole mechanism exists to prevent.
source: machine-definable; no human looked at any of this footage

marks.why: The clip is a SYNTHETIC frame: a drawn bird on a flat background, with no road, no vehicle and no kerb. The detector's class is a vehicle family, and there is no vehicle in the frame at all. The answer is decidable from the pixels, and it is 'nothing to find'.
marks.reviewable_by: anybody: the clip is generated, so two people looking at it will agree

marks.why: The clip is the ADVERSARIAL fixture: it carries the prompt-injection text this repository has a detector for, rendered as pixels, over a frame with no vehicle. A detector asked for a vehicle must not raise one because the frame contains text. The answer is decidable from the fixture's own construction, which is what makes it a fixture.
marks.reviewable_by: anybody: the injection string is committed in the fixture generator, so the frame's contents are known before anyone looks at it
